newsitem.title: TANZANIA: Prices boosted for top grade Tanzanian coffees.
newsitem.headline: Prices boosted for top grade Tanzanian coffees.

text.p: Tanzanian AA and AB grade mild arabicas were buoyant at last week's export auction in the northern town of Moshi, traders said on Monday.
"Thursday was one of the most incredible days at the auction. The highest prices for mild arabicas grade AA sold at $165 per 50 kg bag," a senior trader told Reuters by telephone.
Lower grades sold at prices averaging between $117 and $159.20 per 50 kg.
Tanzania Coffee Board data showed northern arabica prices at $125 for premium AAs and $124 for ABs at the previous auction on October 3. The data showed lower grades at $75-107.
A total of 33,223 60-kg bags of mild washed arabicas and 11,256 bags of robusta were sold at Thursday's auction.
Coffee is measured in 60 kg bags but sold in 50 kg units.
The trader attributed the high prices for Tanzania's premier grades to a general shortage on the world market for mild arabicas in addition to improvements in quality.

"The high prices are in line with the quality. We had some excellent lots, expecially for the double As and ABs which fetched very high prices. I am definitely optimistic. It's a good sign, the quality is there," the trader said.

Another trader reported strong interest from buyers since the Tanzanian coffee auctions resumed with the new 1996/97 season in August, but added that Thursday's "extreme prices" were due to a shortage among certain players.
"I think there is a very strong interest from buyers at the moment, probably because of the shortage of mild arabicas on the world market," the trader told Reuters.
Tanzania holds coffee export auctions twice a month.
